subject: Data Engineering
title: The Small Files Problem
description: A quick, practical guide to The Small Files Problem.

hook.text: The lake has one million files, each 1 KB. A query that should take seconds takes ten minutes.

buildup.text: Each file requires a metadata lookup. A million tiny files means a million lookups before data is even read.

discovery.text: Small files kill lake performance. Query engines spend more time listing files than reading data.

twist.text: Streaming ingestion is the usual culprit. Each micro-batch writes a tiny file, and they accumulate fast.

climax.text: Compaction jobs merge small files into larger ones periodically, restoring query performance.

punchline.text: Small files, big problem. Compact them regularly.

quiz.question: Why do small files hurt data lake query performance?
options: Each file requires a metadata lookup, creating massive overhead
Small files use more storage space
Query engines can only read large files
